prompt:
Write 6 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1313; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment kept growing well beyond what this injury usually needs, with more visits and new services added month after month.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: The claim was opened after a report that the insured's vehicle was struck while turning left at an intersection. The claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact is being routed through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Photos taken at the scene show damage that lines up with the described impact. The driver is named on the policy and the coverage was in force at the time of loss.

Entry 3: The police report and two statements confirm the claimant was in the vehicle, though no independent witnesses have come forward. No earlier damage to the vehicle has been found in our records or in the inspection.

Entry 4: The claimant reports neck and back strain, which is a plausible injury for a collision of this type. No prior injury to the same body area is known from available history.

Entry 5: Treatment has grown steadily over recent months, with more visits and new services added each month, well beyond what this injury usually requires. The claimant has given the same account of the accident in every conversation so far.

Entry 6: Nothing in the file suggests the damage occurred before the coverage started. Review of the treatment billing against typical care for this injury is ongoing, and the file will be referred for a further medical review.
